summary: The builder fix is correct and is the only code change. Acceptance items 1, 3 and 4 hold on my fixtures, and G1 reproduces on this machine. The task goes back for a documentation-level correction. The audit states that filtered rows match the full export 'with identical column names and Arrow types', and a worker test comment says the filtered export is 'not a re-encoding'. checks.area: acceptance 2: whole-observation filtering, shared lineage, known-missing, exclusions
checks.result: pass for membership; failed for the worker's schema claim
checks.evidence: Membership: five observations (passed, failed on the other side of the same IDs, missing required signal, unprofiled task, second pass) split into filtered and ledger by full identity. Filtered rows plus ledger row_count equal the full rows, and the eligible identities in quality.json equal the filtered identities. Separator-like identities ('a|b','c' vs 'a','b|c') stay distinct. Shuffled inputs give byte-identical filtered.parquet. With no profile, nothing passes and everything is ledgered as unchecked. Schema: filtered.parquet is written with pa.Table.from_pandas after to_pandas, so it is a re-encoding. Verified drift: an int64 column with nulls anywhere becomes double; a string column that is null within the eligible subset becomes Arrow null type; large_string becomes string; Parquet schema key-value metadata is dropped; IEEE NaN values in a float signal (as non-pandas writers may store them) become Parquet nulls (15 NaN in, 0 NaN and 15 nulls out). Values still read the same in pandas. Both the audit claim (core02-release-lineage.json line 58) and the test comment (test_release_lineage_adversarial.py line 164) overstate the result.
